title: Playing with Buddy Petit and his style
summary: Burbank recalls Petit's eight-piece band, out-of-town jobs, low-register melodic style and use of mutes, and how a clarinet fits with it.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: For a while. Did you ever play with Buddy Petit? Oh, yeah.
I played with Buddy Petit. At the time I played with Buddy Petit, he had an eight-piece band. And he used to go out of town, all around Muggaloosa. Mm-hmm.
How many, you say, eight pieces that have two trumpets or sax? Oh, yeah.
I had a ten of sax. Henry Harden was playing tenor sax. Mm-hmm. And two trumpets.
Do you know about when that was? Say, would it be around 1925 or a little later or 19, early 1920s? Or any way to remember? Or how old you were when you played with Buddy? No, I don't.
But I think that should have been somewhere around between 25 and 30. Long in that period.
Long in that period.
Long in that period. Mm-hmm.
How was Buddy playing then? Oh, he was playing good.
Really good. Yeah.

Somebody told me once in his later days he didn't play as well as when he was real young. And I just wondered, that was near the end of his life then, wasn't it? Well, no. He played with him, I guess.
He might have not been quite as strong because he drank so hard. But he still was wonderful.
Well, he still was good.
Yeah. He had a different style from anyone I ever heard. His style was all together different.
What was he like? Did he play low or high or? He played low.
He played low.
He ever used mutes or just the open horn mostly or how? Yeah, he used mutes.
Mutes too.
Mostly the do-eby.
Those days, some fellas used the do-eby. All the things that you hear these fellas doing these mutes these days. Them fellas did all that just with the do-eby.
Would you find it would be easier to play with Albert if he was playing down low? You wouldn't have to keep getting over him all the time? Oh yeah, sure. So much easier to work. So much easier.
He played down low on the staff all the time. Wouldn't be getting in your way or something?
No.
No. There's nothing but a lot of chromatics.
Would he stick pretty well, you might say, to the melody so that you could… Yeah.
Oh yeah. Yeah.
Would you like coming down the brakes to sort of bridge it or would you be going over him all the time? How would you play with him? How would you do the do-eby?
Well, I'd just play my regular way, you know.
